region.text: Ubangi-Shari, the French colony within the frontier set by France

ledger.note: 13 August 1960: the Central African Republic becomes independent from France. 'the Central African Republic formally received independence from France on 13 August 1960'; it had 'been a French colony under the name Ubangi-Shari' and was 'granted autonomy 1 December 1958' (infobox 'Republic established: 1 December 1958'). Cliopatria starts the row only in 1961.

4 December 1976: Bokassa proclaims the Central African Empire. He 'named himself Emperor Bokassa I of the Central African Empire on 4 December 1976' ('From 1976 to 1979, the country was known as the Central African Empire'; the infobox dates his coronation 4 December 1977). Same state, land and colour.

21 September 1979: the republic is restored. Infobox 'Bokassa I's overthrow and republic restored: 21 September 1979'; 'In September 1979, France overthrew Bokassa and restored Dacko to power.' Same state, land and colour.

region.text: the north-eastern towns first seized: N'Delé, Sam Ouandja, Ouadda

ledger.note: 10 December 2012: the Séléka rebels seize N'Delé, Sam Ouandja and Ouadda. 'On 10 December 2012, the rebels seized the towns of' N'Delé, Sam Ouandja and Ouadda (the CAR page: 'In November 2012, Séléka, a coalition of rebel groups, took over towns in the northern and central regions'). The page names the towns, not the prefectures: Bamingui-Bangoran and Haute-Kotto are the researcher's reading. The rebels then 'seized the capital in March 2013' (CAR page; they 'reached the Presidential Palace' on 24 March) and Djotodia held the presidency until his resignation on 10 January 2014; the zone stays the north-east.

End of 2014: the fighting becomes a partition. The page gives no end for the contested stage ('A ceasefire was signed on 24 July 2014 in Brazzaville' and others failed): the researcher closes the contested zone when the page reports the country 'de facto partitioned' by the end of 2014, which the loss event records.

region.text: the north and east, held by the ex-Séléka groups

ledger.note: End of 2014: the Central African Republic is partitioned de facto. 'By the end of 2014, the country was de facto partitioned with the Anti-Balaka controlling the south and west', the ex-Séléka groups holding 'the north and east' (CAR page: 'ex-Séléka in the northeast'); the ex-Séléka factions 'controlled about 60% of the country's territory' (undated), 'six rebel groups who together control two-thirds' on 19 December 2020; Séléka leaders declared the autonomous 'Republic of Logone or Dar El Kuti' on 14 December 2015, with Bambari as intended capital. The government 'captured a number of strategic towns throughout February 2021' (Bria, Kaga-Bandoro, the Bakouma sub-prefecture, Nzacko, Bossembele, Bouar, Beloko and Bossangoa): the 2021 reversal is the gain and the contest that follow in this ledger, so the loss stands from the end of 2014 to February 2021; the UPC and 3R signed disarmament agreements on 11 July 2025, after this dossier's last year. The eight prefectures are the researcher's reading of 'the north and east' and cover 62 percent of the country's cells, close to the page's 60 percent.

region.text: Haute-Kotto, Nana-Grébizi and Mbomou, the prefectures of the towns the government captured in February 2021 (Bria, Kaga-Bandoro, the Bakouma sub-prefecture and Nzacko)

ledger.note: February 2021: the government retakes the towns of the ex-Séléka north and east. The government 'captured a number of strategic towns throughout February 2021, including towns of Bria, Kaga-Bandoro, the Bakouma sub-prefecture, Nzacko, Bossembele, Bouar, Beloko and Bossangoa'; 'the rebels have been on the retreat for the first time in years'. The page names towns, not areas: Bria is in Haute-Kotto, Kaga-Bandoro in Nana-Grébizi, Bakouma and Nzacko in Mbomou, and taking the three prefectures whole is the researcher's reading. Bossembele, Bouar, Beloko and Bossangoa lie in the west, outside the eight prefectures of the partition. The month is February, not a day.

region.text: the five prefectures of the 2014 partition not named in the February 2021 captures (Vakaga, Bamingui-Bangoran, Ouaka, Haut-Mbomou, Basse-Kotto)

ledger.note: February 2021: the rest of the ex-Séléka north and east becomes contested ground. The page says the government is advancing and 'the rebels have been on the retreat for the first time in years', that in March 2022 Wagner 'launched a large offensive against armed groups in the northern part of the country' and that 'as the rebels were being pushed back' the Russian adviser urged them to hand over their leaders; it names no town in these five prefectures and gives no front line, so the zone is a bridging reading (confidence 1).

region.text: the five prefectures of the 2014 partition not named in the February 2021 captures (Vakaga, Bamingui-Bangoran, Ouaka, Haut-Mbomou, Basse-Kotto)

ledger.note: End of 2024: the dataset horizon, not an end. The page gives no outcome for these prefectures: four armed groups (MLCJ, RPRC, UFR, UFR-R) announced their dissolution in Bangui on 4 December 2022, and the UPC and 3R signed disarmament agreements on 11 July 2025; no page opened says who held the land in 2023-2024.

wars.name: Central African Republic Bush War
wars.outcome: Ended by the Syrte Agreement (February 2007) and the Birao Peace Agreement (April 2007).
wars.note: 'The Central African Bush War began in 2004'; 'forces opposed to Bozize took up arms against his government'. In November 2006 the rebels 'had taken control of towns in the country's northern regions' (the page; Bozize asked for French military support, French airstrikes followed in December 2006). The page names no town and no region (it names Birao only in 'the Birao Peace Agreement'), so no zone is recorded.

wars.name: Central African Republic Civil War

zones.text: the north and east held by the ex-Séléka groups

wars.outcome: Ongoing at the dataset horizon: Séléka seized the capital in March 2013, Djotodia resigned on 10 January 2014, the country was de facto partitioned by the end of 2014, ceasefires (Libreville 11 January 2013, Brazzaville 24 July 2014, Nairobi 2015, Rome June 2017) and the February 2019 accord with 14 groups did not end it; the government retook strategic towns in February 2021; four groups announced their dissolution in Bangui on 4 December 2022; the UPC and 3R signed disarmament agreements on 11 July 2025.
wars.note: Infobox 'Start date: 10 December 2012 ... Status: Ongoing'; no territorial-change field. The 'to' year is the dataset horizon, not an end. The zone is the whole partition of 2014; from February 2021 the ledger shows the government regaining Haute-Kotto, Nana-Grébizi and Mbomou and contesting the other five.

certainty.note: Frontiers 'established by France' and kept; the pages are silent on any border dispute. The north and east were outside government control from 2014: soft there in fact, but the frontier itself is not in question.

notes: Page budget 2 of 2 (Central African Republic, Central African Republic Civil War). (1) Cliopatria's row starts in 1961; independence was on 13 August 1960 and the French Fifth Republic shape holds the land in 1960: a new 1960 keyframe repeats the 1961 outline and the French dossier (eu-22) should lose the land in 1960. (2) The Séléka rebels are given a rebel dossier ('seleka', added by af-08-g): the pages give a partition with ex-Séléka in 'the north and east' by the end of 2014 and about 60 percent of the territory; the eight prefectures used (Vakaga, Bamingui-Bangoran, Nana-Grébizi, Haute-Kotto, Ouaka, Haut-Mbomou, Mbomou, Basse-Kotto) are the researcher's reading and cover 62 percent of the cells. The government of Djotodia (March 2013-January 2014) held the capital but is not a separate state. The contest_end of December 2014 is a bridging judgement (confidence 1). REPAIR after review: the government's recapture of Bria, Kaga-Bandoro, Bakouma sub-prefecture and Nzacko in February 2021 is now a gain of Haute-Kotto, Nana-Grébizi and Mbomou from seleka (confidence 2: the page names towns, the prefectures are the researcher's reading) and the other five prefectures are contested from February 2021 to the dataset horizon (confidence 1; the pages give no front line, the rebels 'on the retreat', the March 2022 Wagner offensive and the dissolution of four groups on 4 December 2022 are all they say). The dissolutions of 2022 and 2025 are not territorial events. The Bush War of 2004-2007 holds no zone: the page says only 'towns in the country's northern regions'. (3) The Republic of Logone / Dar El Kuti (declared 14 December 2015, intended capital Bambari) is a claim, not a territory held on the pages: it is recorded in the seleka dossier as a rename. (4) The 2014 Cliopatria shape differs from 1961-2013 by 171 km2 with no event on any page.
